cases.name: Barbara J. Cruz
cases.about: Her Go Fund Me said, "Our mother is a dedicated grandmother, nurse, and most importantly a friend and confidant to all her children. Our family has decided to try and establish a scholarship fund for nurses in honor of our mother and our late sister Diana Cruz. Our sister was tragically killed by a drunk driver at the age of 15 on December 14, 1997 while returning from Christmas shopping with friends. After her death our mother established the Diana Cruz Memorial Scholarship fund and has been honoring a deserving student every year since our sister's passing for the last 25 years. Our mother gave the last scholarship award in June of 2023 as her scholarship fund was exhausted. Our mother had expressed the desire to add more money to the scholarship fund during a conversation this summer with my sister. In light of this, we hope to establish a scholarship fund in both their names with any additional funds that are received past the original goal of $10,000. Nursing changed our mother's life for the better. Nurses are patient advocates, and it was in the spirit of advocating for her sister that she lost her life. We are certain that our mother would want us to continue to honor her and our beautiful sister together."

cases.name: Kylee Marie Monteiro
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Kylee was a bright and spirited young woman who graduated from Attleboro High School in 2025. With a passion for welding, she proudly earned her welding certificate and was eagerly looking forward to a promising career in the field. Her vibrant personality shone through her love for posting on the internet and interacting with her friends. Above all, Kylee adored her sisters and niece, cherishing every moment spent with them."
cases.narrative:
On 8/19/2025, her remains were found on his 25-acre property in Rehoboth, MA. 

"Groom initially contacted Rehoboth police on Aug. 8 to report that Monteiro was missing. Groom said she had been at his house looking for a place to stay, they had gotten into an argument and she left, walking down the driveway.

As police continued their investigation, prosecutors said they spoke with Monteiro's sister, who said she was texting her sister on Aug. 6 and Monteiro told her she'd had an altercation with Groom. The sister said Monteiro texted her that "He threw me on the ground and pulled my hair and strangled me. My phone is at 4% and if I die, it was Greg."

The sister later received a response from Monteiro's phone saying she was going to stay at Groom's house.

A search was conducted last Thursday on Groom's property, and though nothing was found, police continued their investigation because family members still hadn't heard from Monteiro.

On Tuesday, prosecutors said Groom returned to the Rehoboth Police Department for another interview, and admitted that on Aug. 6, he got into an altercation with Monteiro and pushed her, causing her to fall backward and hit her head. He said when she tried to contact someone, he knocked her phone out of her hand.

Investigators continued to press Groom, informing him that they had applied for and been granted a search warrant and were set to search his property with cadaver dogs and an excavator.

Given an opportunity to tell police where the body was located, prosecutors said Groom drew a rudimentary map and indicated that he had gotten into an argument behind a shed on his property where he was known to stay and where Monteiro had stayed with him. During the altercation, Groom said he stabbed Monteiro twice in the neck and once in the chest, with the blade breaking off in her chest, killing her.

Groom told investigators he spent several hours digging a hole in the woods 20 yards from where he had killed her. Through the night, he said he pushed Monteiro's body into the hole and covered it up.

Prosecutors said police returned to the scene and found a large pile of brush next to the shed, and blood and other physical evidence were recovered from underneath the pile. About 20 yards away, they found another pile of brush, underneath which they found a 5-foot deep hole containing what they believe to be Monteiro's remains."
